name: Question 20
problem:
Consider a function $g(t)$ such that its Laplace transform is $L{g(t)}=G(s)$ for $s>{s}_{0}.$ Suppose we wish to find $L{{e}^{-3t}g(t)}.$ Select the correct options in the reasoning below.By definition of the Laplace transform, we can write 

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{e}^{-3t}g(t)} & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{{field-1}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{{field-2}}\,g(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={{field-3}}\,\text{for}\,{{field-4}}.\end{aligned}
$$
worked_solution:
Starting from the definition of the Laplace transform, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{e}^{-3t}g(t)} & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{e}^{-st}\cdot {e}^{-3t}\,g(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{e}^{-(s+3)t}\,g(t)\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall that $G(s)={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{e}^{-st}\,g(t)\,\text{d}t,$ where $s>{s}_{0}.$ Therefore, 

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\infty }{e}^{-(s+3)t}\,g(t)\,\text{d}t=G(s+3),
$$

where 

$$
s+3>{s}_{0}\,⇒\,s>{s}_{0}-3.
$$

Question 20

Consider a function g(t) such that its Laplace transform is L{g(t)}=G(s) for s>s0. Suppose we wish to find L{e−3tg(t)}. Select the correct options in the reasoning below.By definition of the Laplace transform, we can write

e−st⋅e−3tg(t)
est⋅e−3tg(t)
e−st⋅e−3tg(t)
est⋅e3tg(t)
e−st⋅e3tg(t)
e−(s+3)t
e(s−3)t
e(s+3)t
e−(s+3)t
e−(s−3)t
G(s+3)
G(s+3)
G(s−3)
G(s)
s>s0−3
s>s0+3
s>s0−3
s>s0
L{e−3tg(t)}=∫0∞{(est⋅e−3tg(t))(S0)}dt=∫0∞{(e(s−3)t)(S1)}g(t)dt={(G(s+3))(S2)}for{(s>s0+3)(S3)}.
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Starting from the definition of the Laplace transform, we have

L{e−3tg(t)}=∫0∞e−st⋅e−3tg(t)dt=∫0∞e−(s+3)tg(t)dt

Now, recall that G(s)=∫0∞e−stg(t)dt, where s>s0. Therefore, ∫0∞e−(s+3)tg(t)dt=G(s+3), where s+3>s0⇒s>s0−3.
